symbols.c_eps: constant c = O((log(1/epsilon))^2) depending on the input parameter epsilon

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: In any stochastic setting with a unique optimal arm, the proposed algorithm achieves R(T) \leq (2(1+\epsilon) + \sum_{i \in [K] \setminus \{ i^* \}} \max\{4\frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} + c \log (1 + \frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i}), 2(1+\epsilon)\}) \log T + o (\log T), where ... \epsilon \in (0, 1/2] is an input parameter for the algorithm, and c = O((\log \frac{1}{\epsilon})^2).

results.notes: Bound has additive o(log T), recorded as limsup of R(T) with the leading term. Regret is max over arms of expected loss difference, equals sum Delta_i P_i in stochastic setting. With epsilon=0.2 the paper states c can be taken as 4.2 and 2(1+eps)=2.4 (Table 3). sigma_i^2 is loss variance.

symbols.h_z: explicit function h(z) = 2(1+eps) for z <= beta0/(2(1+delta/beta0)), else 2z(1+sqrt(1+2delta/z)) - 2delta + 4delta(log(z/beta0)+log(1+sqrt(1+2delta/z))) + beta0^2/z - 2beta0; beta0=1+eps, delta=O(log(1/eps))

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Further, in adversarial settings, the regret for the proposed algorithm satisfies R(T) \leq \sqrt{K \log T \min\left\{ T, 4L^*,  4 (T-L^*),  4 Q_{\infty}  \right\}} + O(K \log T)

results.notes: Leading term has exact constant 1; only the additive K log T term is in O(). R(T) = max_i E[sum loss diff] (expectation of loss difference against fixed arm). Implies worst-case sqrt(KT log T).

symbols.R_sto: RHS of the stochastic bound (2(1+eps) + sum_{i != i*} max{4 sigma_i^2/Delta_i + c log(1+sigma_i^2/Delta_i), 2(1+eps)}) log T + o(log T)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: In addition, in corrupted stochastic settings, we have $R(T) \leq \mathcal{R} + O(\sqrt{C \mathcal{R}})$, where $\mathcal{R}$ is the RHS of \eqref{eq:thm1-bound-sto}.

results.notes: Leading R_sto has coefficient 1; also stated as Proposition 3 (prop:bound-corrupted). Regret measured on corrupted losses; C does not need to be known.

bound.expression_latex: R(T)\leq\sqrt{\frac{K}{1-2\eta}\left(\min\left\{T,4 L^*,4 (T - L^*),4 Q_{\infty},\frac{8}{\eta} V_1\right\}+\frac{K}{\eta}\right)\log T}+O(K \log T)

symbols.Q_inf: min over lbar of E[sum_t ||l(t) - lbar||_inf^2]

source.quote: by modifying the algorithm in the way described in Appendix~\ref{sec:path-length}, we can obtain a regret bound of R(T) \leq \sqrt{\frac{K}{1-2\eta}(\min\{T, 4 L^*, 4 (T - L^*), 4 Q_{\infty}, \frac{8}{\eta} V_1\} + \frac{K}{\eta}) \log T} + O(K \log T) in adversarial settings, where $\eta \in (0, 1 / 2 )$ is an input parameter.

results.notes: Stated in a Remark with proof sketch in Appendix C (relies on Proposition 13 of Ito 2021).

symbols.R_sto: RHS of the stochastic bound in eq. (thm1-bound-sto)

source.quote: In corrupted stochastic settings, this modified algoirthm achieves a regret bound of R(T) \leq  \frac{1}{1-2\eta} \mathcal{R} + O ( \sqrt{ \frac{1}{1-2\eta} C \mathcal{R} } + K \sqrt{\frac{ \log T }{\eta (1-2\eta)}} ), where $\mathcal{R}$ is the RHS of \eqref{eq:thm1-bound-sto}.

results.notes: Leading term R_sto/(1-2eta) has exact coefficient; remainder in O(). C=0 gives stochastic case (Appendix C).

source.label: prop_moment
source.quote: For any $0\le \mu^*<\mu_i\le 1$ and $\sigma_i^2 \le \mu_i(1-\mu_i)$, there exists a loss distribution $\mathcal{D}$ over $[0,1]^K$ such that any consistent algorithm suffers \liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{R(T)}{\log T} \ge \sum_{i\neq i^*} \frac{\Delta_i}{...} and there exists an algorithm achieving this bound with equality for all $\mathcal{D}$.

results.notes: Losses: mu_star is the optimal (smallest) mean loss, mu_i mean losses. This is a simplification of Honda & Takemura (2012) Theorem 4; achievability part is from their Theorem 1. Paper approximates the best (Delta,sigma)-form as sum(2 sigma_i^2/Delta_i + 0.5 log(1+sigma_i^2/Delta_i) + 1) within 6%.
